human_pressure.one_screen_brief: Keep Ailuros as the consumer of a canonical evidence package rather than an EverRun log adapter. Tighten producer-neutral package diagnostics and conformance coverage around manifest.json + timeline.json, required manifest metadata, canonical timeline event envelopes, ISO-8601 timestamps, unknown producer event preservation, and actionable CLI errors. Ailuros must not learn controller-result.json/events.jsonl or legacy EverRun history layouts. Old non-conformant EverRun history remains intentionally unsupported.
human_pressure.why_now: EverRun can own the producer-side export. Ailuros needs a crisp, stable and testable consumer boundary so dogfood works without importing producer internals into governance runtime code.
do_not_misread: This is not an EverRun compatibility importer.
This does not relax evidence validation to accept arbitrary legacy history.
Unknown event types are evidence, not errors by default, as long as the canonical envelope is valid.
Producer-specific semantic interpretation must not leak into generic package validation.
red_lines: Do not add branches keyed on source == everrun that parse EverRun-native files.
Do not read controller-result.json, events.jsonl, execution-report.json or .everrun/history directly.
Do not weaken required package files or required canonical fields merely to make old exports pass.
Do not synthesize governance PASS/ACCEPT/authority/budget facts from missing evidence.
Do not introduce a producer plugin framework or runtime policy engine.

machine_core.goal: Make the canonical evidence-package ingestion boundary explicit, producer-neutral, diagnostically useful and regression-tested for a second producer such as EverRun.
red_lines: No synthetic evidence for missing fields.
No new runtime blocker outside malformed/non-conformant package validation.
invariants: Ailuros owns interpretation of canonical evidence, not reconstruction of producer runtime state.
A canonical package is rejected when required package structure or required envelope fields are malformed.
A valid unknown event_type is preserved through the existing external-evidence path rather than rejected solely for not being in an internal enum.
Producer-neutral validation yields the same result regardless of whether source is EverRun or another conforming producer.

observable_effect.assertion: Any conforming producer package with manifest.json and timeline.json can be audited/imported/projected without Ailuros parsing producer-native runtime files.

proofs.assertion: Second-producer fixtures pass audit -> import -> report/rebuild through the same generic path.
Legacy EverRun controller folders without canonical package files are rejected with actionable generic diagnostics rather than special-case adaptation.

failure_semantics: Missing manifest.json or timeline.json is a package-contract failure with explicit missing-file diagnostics.
Missing required manifest fields is a package-contract failure naming each missing/invalid field.
Malformed event envelopes fail validation with event location/index and field-level reason when possible.
Unknown event_type with a valid envelope is preserved as external evidence, not treated as malformed.
Import/report failure remains a pipeline failure and is not reclassified as a governance decision.

steps.title: Make package structure diagnostics explicit
details: Ensure the external evidence-package validation path clearly requires manifest.json and timeline.json before import.
Return deterministic, producer-neutral diagnostics listing missing required files rather than a generic parse/import failure.
Do not accept EverRun-native controller folders as an alternate package layout.

steps.title: Validate canonical manifest metadata
details: Validate non-empty package_version, source, governance_mode, schema_version, run_id and generated_at.
Require generated_at to be parseable as a complete timezone-aware ISO-8601 timestamp.
Keep validation generic: source value may identify EverRun, but validation behavior must not branch into EverRun parsing.

steps.title: Validate canonical timeline envelopes
details: For every timeline entry require non-empty event_id, event_type and timestamp plus a payload object.
Require event timestamp to be a complete timezone-aware ISO-8601 value.
Report malformed event index/event_id where available so producers can fix exports quickly.

steps.title: Preserve unknown producer event types
details: Confirm that a valid event_type outside Ailuros internal enums is retained through the existing EXTERNAL_EVIDENCE/external-evidence normalization path.
Do not create a new internal enum member for every producer telemetry event.
Known shared governance event types continue to project into their existing semantic paths; unknown types remain inspectable external evidence.

steps.title: Improve CLI audit/import diagnostics
details: Make evidence-audit/import-evidence-package style commands surface missing files, missing fields, malformed timestamps and duplicate event IDs in concise human-readable output.
Preserve machine-readable/non-zero failure behavior for invalid packages.
Do not add recovery that silently manufactures canonical fields from producer-native files.

steps.title: Lock second-producer conformance with fixtures
details: Extend the existing fixtures/runtime-evidence/second-producer coverage with one valid canonical package and focused invalid variants for missing file, missing manifest field, malformed timestamp, duplicate event_id and malformed payload.
Include at least one unknown producer event_type in the valid fixture and prove it survives as external evidence.
Prove the valid fixture can traverse evidence audit, import and report/rebuild using the production path without source-specific code.

acceptance: A conforming second-producer package containing manifest.json and timeline.json validates and imports through the generic production path.
Required manifest metadata is enforced with field-specific diagnostics.
Timeline event envelopes enforce event_id/event_type/timestamp/payload, timezone-aware ISO-8601 timestamps and package-local unique IDs.
Unknown producer event types are preserved as external evidence.
A raw/legacy EverRun controller directory is rejected as non-conformant without invoking an EverRun adapter.
CLI diagnostics are clear enough for a producer implementation to identify the exact package defect.
Existing governance projections and full regression suite remain green.

must_check: The implementation remains producer-neutral and contains no EverRun-native parser.
manifest.json + timeline.json canonical structure is explicitly validated.
The six required manifest fields are enforced and generated_at is timezone-aware ISO-8601.
Every event requires event_id/event_type/timestamp/payload and IDs are unique within the package.
Unknown valid event types survive through external-evidence normalization.
Invalid package diagnostics are precise and useful from CLI entry points.
Second-producer conformance proves audit/import/report without source-specific branches.
Validation passes and forbidden files are untouched.
reject_if: A source == everrun branch parses controller-result.json, events.jsonl, execution-report.json or legacy history.
Missing canonical files or fields are filled from guesses or producer-native artifacts.
Unknown event types are rejected solely because they are absent from an Ailuros enum.
The change creates a producer adapter registry/plugin framework for this single need.
Governance rules are weakened merely to make the fixture pass.
Validation fails or forbidden files are changed.

validation_notes.targeted_contract_coverage: Exercises the second-producer canonical evidence-package boundary and the CLI-facing failure modes while keeping the full suite as regression proof.
